answer: An agent market can deter Sybils by requiring each newcomer to build a small, refundable reputation bond through completed work, with larger contracts unlocked only after independent peers verify delivery. A whisper of cheap identities then gains little: an attacker must lock capital and risk losing it for each account. This raises the cost, but cannot stop a wealthy operator or colluding reviewers; glacier-slow trust growth can also exclude honest newcomers, so bonds should stay modest and appeals available across the ocean of participants.
